review_notes: I read the whole file and the planeForm definition in Moments.lean. I grepped for uses of directionProjection and compressedTriangle across the Interpolation directory (TorusJets.lean, PrimitiveDirections.lean). The file has no @[simp] declarations and no simp-set conflicts or loops. The one issue is that directionProjection has no simp or unfolding lemma, so each use unfolds the definition by name. I did not run Lean, so I cannot say what the proposed lemma would do to the existing simp calls. I left planeForm unchanged because its uses are mostly in another file and the benefit there is less clear.

findings.excerpt:
def directionProjection (i j : ℤ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : ℝ :=
  (i : ℝ) * p.2 - (j : ℝ) * p.1
findings.problem: directionProjection is a bare def with no simp or unfolding lemma, such as one for its value at a pair (x, y). Every use unfolds it by name instead: `simp [directionProjection]`, `simp [directionProjection, div_eq_mul_inv]`, and `dsimp [planeForm, directionProjection] at *` in this file, and `dsimp [directionProjection]` and `dsimp [directionProjection, A]` in TorusJets.lean. The `at *` form unfolds every hypothesis, including unrelated ones. The `simp [directionProjection, div_eq_mul_inv]` call also rewrites the target with a global division-to-inverse rule only to close one endpoint goal. A canonical normal form for the evaluation at explicit points like (x, 0) or (0, y) is therefore rebuilt by hand each time.
findings.proposed_change: Add a pair-evaluation lemma, for example `@[simp] theorem directionProjection_mk (i j : ℤ) (x y : ℝ) : directionProjection i j (x, y) = (i : ℝ) * y - (j : ℝ) * x := rfl`. Optionally add a `directionProjection_apply` lemma for a general p. The existing uses can then call `simp` or `rw [directionProjection_mk]`. Replace `dsimp [planeForm, directionProjection] at *` with `dsimp only [planeForm, directionProjection_apply] at hy ⊢` or similar. This makes the unfolding direction uniform and removes the need to add `div_eq_mul_inv` to the call at line 162. The lemma terminates because its right-hand side contains no directionProjection.
findings.benefit: The unfolding of directionProjection is stated once, in one direction. Proofs in PrimitiveDirections.lean and TorusJets.lean stop depending on definitional unfolding at `*` and on extra global simp lemmas. Later changes to the definition are then confined to one lemma.
